comparator.name: Medicine
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official TER defines a compulsory 180-EC Bachelor of Medicine organized into Causes of Diseases, longitudinal Knowledge Development and Competency Development. Competency Development is delivered through one of four Learning Communities: Sustainable Care, Intramural Care, Innovative Healthcare or Global Healthcare. The medical-knowledge curriculum is common across the routes, and current official evidence does not establish one Learning Community as more representative or more general. Sustainable Care is therefore instantiated through the official-order tie-break because it is listed first in the TER. The selected coherent pathway preserves all 60 EC in each year and contains no minor or free-elective space within the 180-EC degree. The current study guide places Bachelor Project preparation/proposal in Competency Development 3.1 and project execution, individual thesis, reflection and presentation in 3.2. The approved proposal is prerequisite. Research is conducted in teams of 3–5 students with individual competency assessment; the project is embedded in the existing competency blocks, not a separate credited thesis added to 180 EC. The guide was rechecked on 2026-10-08; the original UCR assessment date/evidence remain.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Medicine target offers four Learning Communities for the Competency Development components while retaining one common medical-knowledge curriculum. Current official evidence does not identify one community as the broad default or academically dominant route. Sustainable Care is therefore selected neutrally because it is listed first in the 2026-2027 TER, without reference to UCR fit.

core: Biomedical foundations, disease mechanisms, physiology, anatomy, pharmacology and integrated medical knowledge
Diagnosis, treatment decisions and longitudinal clinical reasoning
Scientific training, epidemiology, statistics, evidence evaluation and medical research
Patient-centred health, behaviour, illness experience and shared decisions
Medical consultation, communication, teamwork and interprofessional collaboration
Prevention, healthy ageing, population health and healthcare innovation
Professional development, ethics, rights and responsibility
Supervised patient contact, care placements and physician competencies
adjacent: Patient health, behaviour and healthcare communication
Public health, prevention and healthy ageing
questions: How do biological mechanisms produce disease and treatment effects?
How do behaviour, communication and social context shape patient health and care?
How can prevention and population evidence support healthy ageing?

selection.assessment: Three complete related-fields programmes are defensible. The closest route studies biomedical disease mechanisms and research; the second studies patient health, behaviour and communication; the third studies public health, prevention and healthy ageing. All pairwise comparisons exceed the 30-EC floor. Production stops at the maximum of three while preserving the absent clinical, consultation, placement and physician-competency sequence explicitly.

alternatives.label: Biomedical disease mechanisms & medical research
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by life science, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, immunity, pathology, epidemiology, laboratory work and evidence synthesis. The label states those academic strengths without presenting the route as Medicine or clinical training.
alternatives.concept: Study disease through molecular and cellular biology, physiology, anatomy, biochemistry, pharmacology, immunity, pathology, epidemiology, laboratory work, psychology and quantitative evidence. This related-fields route examines disease mechanisms and biomedical research but does not teach clinical reasoning under medical supervision, diagnosis, treatment decisions, medical consultation or patient care.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes all dependent life-science and biomedical courses; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes advanced psychology and cognition. Research Methods & Statistics precedes advanced statistics and evidence synthesis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned terms pass; ten courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Patient health, behaviour & healthcare communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines psychology, neuroscience, sociology, epidemiology, communication, leadership, ethics, rights and research methods. The label accurately describes patient-related academic study while avoiding any claim to medical consultation or clinical-care competence.
alternatives.concept: Study psychological, biological and social influences on health, illness and patient experience together with communication, decision-making, teamwork, diversity, ethics, epidemiology and research methods. This route responds to patient-centred medicine and collaborative care as academic questions but provides no medical examination, diagnosis, treatment, supervised consultation or clinical placement.
alternatives.distinctness: The biomedical route and patient-health route share fourteen courses. Each contains ten different courses / 75 EC: the second replaces molecular-cell, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory, pharmacology, immunity and pathology depth with social psychology, leadership, communication, sociology, qualitative research, AI ethics, organisational psychology and behavioural decision-making.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes advanced psychology and cognition, while Research Methods & Statistics precedes statistics, organisational psychology, diversity leadership and behavioural economics. Introductory sociology, psychology, leadership and communication precede advanced qualitative, persuasive and organisational work. All formal prerequisites and exact planned terms pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Public health, prevention & healthy ageing
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is centred on epidemiology, health psychology, lifespan development, prevention, population evidence, public economics, social determinants, ethics, rights and public communication. Climate-related health and communication form a bounded supporting strand rather than the programme description as a whole.
alternatives.concept: Study population health, prevention and healthy ageing through epidemiology, physiology, infection and immunity, health psychology, lifespan development, behavioural decision-making, economics, sociology, ethics, rights and public communication. The route also examines environmental health pressures and collaborative prevention, but it does not provide clinical medicine, physician competencies or supervised care.
alternatives.distinctness: The public-health route shifts the organising level from biomedical mechanisms or individual patient interaction to population evidence, prevention, lifespan health, public economics, social determinants, rights and public communication. It has eight courses / 60 EC not present in the patient-health route and eleven courses / 82.5 EC not present in the biomedical route.
progression: Biomedical, epidemiology, psychology, sociology, economics, communication and research foundations precede physiology, immunity, health psychology, lifespan development, public economics, molecular pathology, persuasive communication, evidence synthesis and behavioural economics. All formal prerequisites and exact planned terms pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

blocks: Biomedical foundations, disease mechanisms & treatment science
Human Physiology addresses important physiological and metabolic foundations within this integrated module, while not reproducing its clinical reasoning or treatment scope.
Infection & Immunity directly addresses host–pathogen interaction, inflammation and immune disease within the broader integrated medical module.
Mechanisms of Disease addresses organ-system pathology and disease mechanisms relevant to ischemia, without clinical diagnostic or treatment training.
Molecular Pathology & Genetics directly addresses neoplasia, cellular injury and molecular disease within this broader integrated endocrine, blood and neoplasm module.
Medical & Health Psychology directly examines health behaviour, illness experience and intervention relevant to healthy-ageing work, but not medical consultation competence.
Lifespan Developmental Psychology addresses ageing, vulnerability and development across the lifespan as one part of this broader medical module.
Persuasive Communication contributes evidence on framing and communication in public and interpersonal settings, but does not provide supervised medical consultation training.

notes.text: Groningen Medicine integrates biomedical knowledge with longitudinal clinical reasoning, medical consultation, supervised patient contact, placements, professional formation and national progress testing. UCR can offer coherent related programmes in biomedical disease research, patient health and communication, or population health and prevention, but none is a Medicine degree or route to physician qualification.

UCR has no clinical-medicine sequence, supervised patient contact, medical examination, diagnosis and treatment training, medical consultation pathway, care placement, physician-competency programme or whole-programme medical progress testing. Biomedical, psychology, public-health, communication and ethics courses remain bounded related contributions rather than substitutes for those components.
